text.title: HealthTech FHIR BA Pack — Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete pack for a remote blood-pressure monitoring dashboard under HIPAA and GDPR, with a note on every value a reader might question, and one symptom-checker pack that breaks six subject rules and what the validator and the privacy officer say about it.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: A digital-health vendor adds a remote blood-pressure monitoring dashboard: patients upload cuff readings from a phone app, clinicians see trends, reminders go out by SMS, and a de-identified copy feeds an outcomes study. US and EU tenants share the platform, so HIPAA and GDPR both apply. The BA runs steps 1-9 of `content/04-procedure.xml` and hands the privacy officer the pack below.

example.title: Complete pack, one blocking processor
example.note: Blood pressure maps to `Observation.component.value[x]` twice, once per LOINC component (8480-6 systolic, 8462-4 diastolic), rather than to one "bp" string: US Core's vital-signs profile is component-based, and the two rows are what an EHR bundle expects.

Sentry is `status: blocking` with `baa_signed: false` and appears verbatim in `blocking_findings`: the contract refuses `cleared` for a PHI-in-scope processor without a BAA, and the error tracker was receiving `Patient.identifier` in request bodies. The fix is either the BAA or scrubbing identifiers from error payloads; the pack does not pretend it is done.

Snowflake has `phi_in_scope: false` and no BAA: the analytics flow feeding it is `safe-harbor` with the method named (all 18 identifier classes, dates to year, zip to 3 digits), so what reaches Snowflake is not PHI. The flow row is the evidence the processor row relies on.

The overlap matrix honours 72 hours for breach notice and 30 days for access for every tenant: the stricter clock of each regime is applied platform-wide rather than per tenant, which is cheaper than two runbooks and is what the rule asks for.

Treatment and research consent are two records with different `text_version` values and the research record has an end date and a `deny` provision on free-text notes; the IRB protocol and approval date sit beside them, and `waiver_of_consent` is false because participants consent themselves.
`audit_trail.application_roles_with_update_or_delete` is an empty list, which the schema caps at zero items: the way to prove append-only is to show no role can rewrite the log.

example.title: Six subject rules broken
example.note: What the validator prints: `element_map[0]: missing required field: binding` on a coded `Observation.code` (r-coded-terminology-bindings); `data_flows[1].de_identification: 'none' not in allowed enum` and `missing required field: de_identification_method` on the model-training flow (r-phi-minimum-necessary-per-flow); `processors[0].status: 'cleared' is not the required const 'blocking'` on an LLM API receiving names with no BAA (r-baa-or-dpa-per-processor); `<root>: missing required field: overlap_matrix` with both regimes true (r-hipaa-gdpr-overlap-matrix-minimum-rows); `consent: missing required field: irb` with research_use true (r-consent-as-fhir-consent-with-irb-reference); `audit_trail.fields: 3 items is under minItems 6`, `append_only: False is not the required const True`, `retention_years: 1 is below minimum 6`, `per_patient_query: False` (r-audit-trail-append-only-six-years); `encryption.stores[0].status: 'cleared'` on an unencrypted transcript bucket and `hops[0].tls_min: '1.0' not in allowed enum` (r-phi-encrypted-transit-and-rest).

What the privacy officer sees beyond the validator: the one consent record has scope "I agree to the terms" and a permit-all provision, so the study cannot show which patients consented to what; and `blocking_findings` is empty while the LLM API, the training bucket and the transcript store are each a reportable violation on day one. The pack goes back to step 2 of the procedure.

list.item: The processor list is only as honest as the flow table: a processor is "not PHI" only when the flow row that feeds it names the de-identification method.
Blocking status is a schema consequence, not a judgement call — phi_in_scope true plus baa_signed false forces it, so a pack cannot clear a vendor on its compliance page.
The audit-trail proof is the absence of a role that can rewrite the log; listing "append-only" as a word is not evidence.
